S.G.Pandit, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimants and owner of the offending vehicle are before this Court in the above two appeals,
questioning the correctness or otherwise of the Judgment and award dated 21.07.2016 in MVC No.1042/2015 on the file of the VIII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi.

entities.text: VIII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimants are before this Court not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded and praying for enhancement of the compensation.
The owner of the vehicle is in appeal aggrieved by saddling of the entire liability.

2. Heard learned counsel Sri. G.R.Turamari, for the claimants, learned counsel Sri. Vitthal S. Teli,
for the owner of the offending vehicle, learned Sri. Gangadhar S. Hosakeri for the Insurance company and perused the materials on record.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, the claimants i.e. the wife, children and the mother of the deceased Sri. Ashok, filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation for the death of Sri. Ashok in a road traffic accident that has occurred on 21.02.2015 involving the lorry bearing registration No.KA-22/A-8990 and TVS XL Luna bearing registration No.KA-49/K-70.

It is stated that, the deceased was aged 55 years and was doing agriculture and earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month, which he was contributing towards the maintenance of his family and further it is also stated that, the deceased was earning more than Rs.1,50,000/- per annum by cooking at various functions.
On issuance of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared though its counsel and filed their objection.
The respondent No.1 - owner of the offending lorry filed statement denying the claim petition averments.

It is also stated in the objection that, the accident Shivappa vs Smt.Sumitra on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126928751/
3 has caused solely due to the negligence of the riding of the TVS XL Luna by the deceased himself.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2- Insurance company apart from denying the claim petition averments, contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
It is also contended that the accident took place solely due to the negligence of the rider of the TVS XL Luna by the rider i.e. the deceased.
Before the tribunal, the claimant No.2 i.e. son of the deceased examined himself as P.W.1, apart from marking Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
On behalf of respondents, two witnesses were examined as R.W.1 and R.W.2, apart from marking Ex.R.1 to R.6(a).

The tribunal based on the material on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.7,33,000/-,
with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

While awarding the above compensation, the tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month by applying multiplier of '11' and deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased, but saddled the entire liability on the respondent No.1 - owner, holding that the driver of the lorry had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
4. Learned counsel Sri. Vitthal S. Teli, for the owner of the offending vehicle would submit that, the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. lorry was having valid and effective driving license to drive the light motor vehicle which is placed on record as Ex.R.4, but he submits that, there was no transport endorsement on the driving licence.
5.

Learned counsel would submit that, the tribunal without looking into material on record,
particularly Ex.R.3 and Ex.R.4 proceeded to saddle the liability on the owner of the offending vehicle.
Learned counsel would submit that, since there is endorsement to drive tractor-trailer, the tribunal ought to have considered the same and saddled the liability on the Insurance company.

Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal filed by the owner.
6.

Learned counsel Sri. G.R.Turamari, appearing for the claimants would submit that, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the lower side and further he submits that, the income assessed by the tribunal at Rs.6,000/- per month of the deceased is on the lower side since it is claimed that the deceased was earning more than Rs.10,000/- by doing agricultural work.

Further the learned counsel would submit that, the tribunal has also committed an error in not granting compensation under the head of future prospects which the claimants would be entitle for additional 10% of the assessed income.
Learned counsel would submit that, the tribunal has committed an error in deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased.
He submits that,
since the dependents of the deceased were five, the tribunal ought to have deducted 1/4th of the assessed income.

Learned counsel would submit that, in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the claimants would be entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Spousal, Parental and Filial consortium.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal.

7. Learned counsel Sri. Gangadhar Hosakeri, appearing for the respondent-Insurance company would submit that, the tribunal is justified in saddling the liability on the respondent No.1-owner of the offending vehicle, since the driver of the offending lorry had no valid and effective driving licence.

It is submitted that, the driver of the offending vehicle has placed on record at Ex.R.6 which discloses that the driver had licence to drive LMV with an endorsement to drive tractor-trailer, but Shivappa vs Smt.Sumitra on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126928751/
4 when the offending vehicle is a heavy goods vehicle having load capacity of 9590 and laden weight of 16200, requires licence to drive the heavy motor vehicle with a transport endorsement.
Thus, he submits that, the owner would not be entitled for any relief before this Court.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal filed by the owner of the offending vehicle.
8. Learned counsel for the Insurance company would further submit that, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is just compensation, which needs no interference.
Further, he submits that, no material is placed on record to establish the income of the deceased and as such, he submits that the claimants would not be entitled for enhanced compensation.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the records, the following points would arise for our consideration :
(i) Whether the tribunal is justified in saddling the liability on respondent No.1 -owner of the offending vehicle?
(ii) Whether the claimants would be entitle for enhanced compensation ?
10. Answer to the above points would be in the affirmative for the following reasons:
The accident that took place on 21.02.2015 involving the vehicles bearing registration No.KA-49/K-70 and KA- - 10 - 22/A-8990, resultant death of Ashok i.e. husband of the first claimant is not in dispute in this appeal.
11. The owner of the offending vehicle i.e. lorry is before this Court in MFA No.103164/2016 questioning the saddling of the liability on him.

Ex.R.3 is the certified copy of the Form KMV 45,
which is issued by the Regional Transport Authority.
It clearly reveals that the laden weight of the lorry was 16200 kgs. and load capacity was 9590 kgs, which means the vehicle is a heavy transport vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle had only light motor vehicle licence, with an endorsement to drive tractor-trailer.
There is no endorsement to drive the transport vehicle or heavy goods vehicle.
In the absence of licence to drive heavy goods vehicle, it is to be considered as a case of no licence to drive the vehicle.
Therefore, the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Devangan Vs. Oriengal Insurance Company Limited, would have no application to the facts of the present case.

Since it is a case for no licence in terms of the decision of the full Bench of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Yallavva and another, reported in Shivappa vs Smt.Sumitra on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126928751/

sentences.text: Therefore, the Insurance company is liable to make payment of the compensation to the claimants at the first instance with liberty to recover the same from the owner.
12. The income assessed by the tribunal at Rs.6,000/- per month of the deceased is on the lower side.
It is claimed that, the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
But the claimants have not placed on record any cogent material to establish the income of the deceased.
In the absence of any material to establish the income, it is for this Court to assess the income notionally.
The notional income assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side.
This Court as well the Lok Adalaths while - 12 - settling the accident claims of the year 2015 would normally assess the income at Rs.8,000/- per month.
Thus, it would be appropriate to assess the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.
The tribunal committed an error in not granting compensation under the head of future prospects.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, has made it clear that, wherever the deceased was aged between 50 to 60 years, the claimants would be entitle for addition of 10% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the deceased was aged 55 years, it would be appropriate to add 10%
towards future prospects.
For the age of 55 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '11' which the tribunal has correctly applied.
There were five dependents on the deceased, it would be appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the assessed income towards the personal expenses of the deceased.

Hence, the loss of dependency would be as under:
- 13 - Rs.8,000/- (10% additional) = Rs.8,800/- X 1/4th deduction = Rs.2,200/- =
Rs.6,600/-.
Rs.6,600/- X 12 X 11 = Rs.8,71,200/-
13.
The claimants are the wife, children and mother of the deceased.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others,
reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, has made it clear that, the dependents such as wife, children and parents would be entitle for spousal, parental and filial consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each.
Thus, the claimants would be entitle for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of consortium, apart from Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
